body: NIST DLMF section 27.3 (Multiplicative Properties) says: "Except for \nu\left(n\right) , \Lambda\left(n\right) , p_{n} , and \pi\left(x\right) , the functions in § 27.2 are multiplicative , which means f(1)=1 and If f is multiplicative, then the values f(n) for n>1 are determined by the values at the prime powers. Specifically, if n is factored as in ( 27.2.1 ), then A function f is completely multiplicative if f(1)=1 and Examples are \left\lfloor 1/n\right\rfloor and \lambda\left(n\right) , and the Dirichlet characters, defined in § 27.8 . If f is completely multiplicative, then ( 27.3.2 ) becomes" Equation 27.3.1 on the page has alt text "f(mn)=f(m)f(n),". Equation 27.3.2 on the page has alt text "f(n)=\prod_{r=1}^{\nu\left(n\right)}f(p^{a_{r}}_{r}).". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
